summary: Former Trinity National Forest lookout on Dubakella Mountain, Trinity County, CA; staffed 1921-1932; a 1961 survey found its wood lookout house partly torn down; listed gone.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; the 1961 survey described the wood lookout house as partly torn down

events.note: Fire started by a hunter who had become lost reached about a quarter acre; lookout W.C. Duncan saw the smoke and was sent to it
W.C. Duncan named as lookout on Dubakella Mt. in a November 1921 newspaper report
New telephone line completed from Peanut to the Dubakella lookout station
Lookout W. Duncan named as the lookout for a visibility study planned by Assistant Forest Supervisor James Farley (excerpt dated 7 September 1932)
Coast and Geodetic Survey description: wood lookout house no longer used by the Forest Service as a lookout; building partly torn down

notes_for_editor: Record kind 'ground' agrees with FFLA and with the NGS wood lookout house description; no correction. The 1921 name W.C. Duncan and the 1932 name W. Duncan are assumed to be one lookout; sources do not say so, so the story uses both names as written. No build date found in the sources read. The 1921, 1931 and 1932 items are newspaper excerpts transcribed on Forest Lookouts, not checked against the papers. One WebSearch lead (a 2021 fire map labelling a Post Creek Lookout nearby) is unconfirmed and not used. No current condition or access source found. Story omits the fined hunter's name. Fact-check 2026-10-10: added the James Farley and 'intending to hunt' evidence quotes, which the story's claims rest on; the story now cites the NGS survey as well as Forest Lookouts for the former-site claim. Two sentences that followed the excerpt's or survey's wording (the 1931 telephone line and the 1961 survey description) were reworded. No other corrections.
